PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). This package is model-authored and unreviewed: driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null, no human reviewed or tested anything, and no hardware was attached or run. The read-only clone stayed at 01df1f18f7e532afda0a38169356fa637d24e432 and was not modified.

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card names family mujoco and helper MujocoDriver because the repository vendors Meta-World MuJoCo assets, but the first confirmed entry symbol is a Gym task class, not one raw MJCF model. SawyerNutAssemblyEnvV2.reset() returns a dictionary observation and step(action) returns (observation, reward, done, info) with a four-element normalised action (envs/sawyer_xyz_env.py:164-167 and :486-488); a MujocoDriver serves one MJCF model through model_path and data.ctrl per actuator, while sawyer_assembly_peg.xml has only two gripper actuators and moves the hand through a mocap weld (third_party/metaworld/metaworld/envs/assets_v2/sawyer_xyz/sawyer_assembly_peg.xml:22-28), so it cannot express the task interface. The package is therefore a GymnasiumDriver (the bridge accepts the legacy gym API) over envs.tasks.sawyer_assembly_peg_v2:SawyerNutAssemblyEnvV2 and binds the card's cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1; the bridge also serves cap.world.seed.v1. The card's other entry symbol wrappers:make_wrapped_env is a factory, not a class: it selects the goal-hidden subclass (wrappers.py:83-87) and applies optional factor wrappers (envs/factors/utils.py:61-72). This package serves the task class with the goal-hidden configuration (envs/env_dict.py:348-355); the factor wrappers, which generate different MJCF XML, are not served. The card's other task classes are separate devices and are not served.

WHY A FAKE: MuJoCo 2.1, mujoco_py and gym are not installed where the gate runs (conda_env.yml:19-46), and package code never imports the clone. backends['fake'] is the package's pure-Python kinematic stand-in (.fake:FakeSawyerNutAssemblyEnvV2); no sim backend is declared because the class is not registered with gym.make and the upstream MuJoCo stack was never run. The fake implements only action_space, observation_space, dt, seed, reset, step and close, all members of the native class and its clone bases (G7 passed).

NOT COVERED: the MuJoCo rigid-body state behind the 39-element proprio observation (qpos, qvel, contacts, the mocap weld, the two gripper actuators and object physics), the assembly reward and success flag, the image array (None because the class default get_image_obs is false), and the factor-generated MJCF variants. The fake returns the full 39-element proprio array, not a reduced one; its start positions, object point, goal point and reward are placeholder test data, each marked # placeholder. The fake is not MuJoCo and was not compared with the upstream environment.

FIDELITY: engine factor-world:assembly-v2/SawyerNutAssemblyEnvV2, level F0, determinism seeded with seed_control none (the configured task has random_init false, so reset_model uses fixed start positions; the legacy seed is recorded but does not select a different start), timestep_ms 12.5 (0.0025 s timestep times frame_skip 5), realtime_factor 0, clock lockstep, reset full, snapshot_restore false (the class has set_state but no get_state pair). The driver's fidelity.gaps lists every difference.

WARNINGS kept from the last gate run: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (the bridge stores the seed for the next reset; the capability itself makes no native call, and the legacy seed() is reached at reset) and G8.NO_UNIT x4 for the bridge-derived inputs ticks, action.values[*] and seed in reset and seed; these are expected for a Gymnasium family driver per PLAYBOOK section 8 and the exemplar README. There were no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings. No site-limits.example.json is needed because the driver declares no operator-required limit, and no catalogue_requests because the package uses only the existing cap.world.reset.v1, cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.seed.v1 classes.

TESTING: test_driver.py keeps the check_driver(HERE, backend='fake') call and adds eight cases (the action space is the envelope, a step reaches the fake and moves the hand, the v2 observation is 39 elements, the legacy seed path, the seed class sets the next reset, the 500-step episode end, the published fidelity contract, and the e-stop latch); all pass. The last gate run passed G1-G9 with only the two expected warning codes above, and check-report.json is the report of that run. RESULT.json was written last and no other file was changed afterwards.
